title: AXI4 4 KB Boundary Check
description: Trace the derived addresses of an illegal four-beat INCR burst, then compare the two legal transactions that keep every transferred byte inside one 4 KB region.

violations.message: The derived beat address enters the 0x1000–0x1FFF region, so the original burst crosses a 4 KB boundary.

annotations.message: The accepted controls declare four INCR transfers of up to four bytes, beginning at 0x0FF8.
Beat B1 at 0x0FFC remains in the original 4 KB region and its final byte is 0x0FFF.
Beat B2 starts at 0x1000. Even though that address is aligned, entering a second 4 KB region makes the declared burst illegal.
The remaining derived address confirms the transaction spans two independently decoded regions; a compliant master must not issue it.
Legal split A is a separate two-beat burst at 0x0FF8 and 0x0FFC, entirely below the boundary.
Legal split B is a new two-beat transaction beginning at 0x1000. Each accepted burst now stays within one 4 KB region.
